pages.summary: Treat this chapter as project intent, not a restaurant’s corporate claims. Keep the interface focused on exploring eight examples and saving a private, editable demo order.

pages.title: Brand Values
pages.summary: Use clarity, visible continuity and honest feedback as design principles. These guide the demo’s expression; they are not claims about a commercial business.

examples.text: “Cantidad de Pastor” names the field directly. “Quitar” removes a line explicitly.

pages.title: Tone of Voice
pages.summary: Write interface copy in clear Spanish with short verbs and sentence case. Be cheerful in discovery and calm in recovery; avoid jokes around errors or persistence.

examples.text: “Elige tu taco” and “Añadir y ver pedido” name the next action without suggesting payment.

examples.text: “No pudimos guardar el cambio. Conservamos tu edición.” Follow with “Reintentar”.

examples.text: Do not use “Compra ahora”, “Te lo llevamos” or “El mejor taco de la ciudad”.

pages.title: Brandmark
pages.summary: The mark combines a clean semicircle, straight base and three geometric filling shapes. Preserve its proportions, internal colors and full 160 × 160 canvas.

pages.title: Logo misuse
pages.summary: Never stretch, rotate, crop, outline or add effects to the logo. Keep the name exact and avoid restaurant badges, invented founding dates and ornamental frames.

examples.text: Do not replace Taquería Monterey with “Monterrey”, remove the accent or use a shortened name as the main signature.

examples.text: No shadows, gradients, cream plaques or curved lettering around the tortilla.

pages.title: Typography
pages.summary: Introduce type with one expressive Bricolage Grotesque heading and quiet Atkinson Hyperlegible support. Use scale and spacing—not extra font families—to create energy.

pages.summary: Bricolage Grotesque carries the name and headings; Atkinson Hyperlegible carries reading, prices and controls. Real files for both families are supplied.

pages.summary: Use Bricolage Grotesque for the brand and short headlines at 36–64 px. Keep natural Spanish capitalization and compact spacing without closing counters or accents.

pages.title: Typography
pages.summary: Use Bricolage 700 for headings and Atkinson 400/700 for body and emphasis. The wordmark targets 800; no 800 file is supplied, so use an explicit 700 fallback, never synthetic bold.

pages.summary: Use Atkinson Hyperlegible at 16 px or larger for body and inputs, 14 px for buttons and 12 px only for secondary notes. Give every label enough room to remain complete.

pages.summary: Use one page heading, clear category headings and quieter product details. Keep total and main action adjacent; do not compete with them through oversized secondary labels.

pages.title: Layouts
pages.summary: Use the sequence header → Maíz poster → Uva action band → grouped menu → shared-edge order. Space with 4/8/12/16/24/32/48 px increments; never overlay fields or illustrations.

pages.title: Colors
pages.summary: Use five exact colors to separate presentation, reading and action. Keep Blanco as the canvas; do not introduce cream backgrounds or additional decorative hues.

pages.title: Using Tints
pages.summary: Keep identity fills solid and exact. Create quieter areas through white space and thinner borders, not new pastel tokens, faded text or translucent brandmarks.

pages.summary: Build graphics from the tortilla arc and a straight shared edge. Keep contours intact and reserve the 8 px, 160 ms alignment movement for a successfully saved addition.

pages.title: Icons
pages.summary: Use simple interface icons with consistent stroke weight and visible labels where meaning is not obvious. Keep every touch target at least 44 px and separate icons from the brandmark.

pages.title: Product illustrations
pages.summary: Replace photography with eight complete conceptual SVG illustrations. Use Uva contours, exact palette fills and shared safe margins; never imply real portions or add unlisted ingredients.

pages.title: Moodboard
pages.summary: Choose the product poster connected to the order as the governing composition. Compare arrangements through scale, edges and control clarity rather than borrowed restaurant imagery.

examples.text: An illustrated tablecloth crowds controls. An order-first opening lacks introduction. Split heroes and repeated sales cards weaken recognition.

brandbook.voice: Español claro, alegre y directo. Acciones concretas: Añadir, Mi pedido y Confirmar pedido de ejemplo. Una nota breve identifica la demo; los estados de guardado son honestos, sin promesas comerciales ni lenguaje técnico innecesario.
brandbook.positioning: Propuesta de identidad original para la demo ficticia de Esteban en Constructor. Un menú breve de tacos y bebidas permite explorar productos ilustrados y guardar pedidos de ejemplo, sin representar un restaurante operativo.
